description: Composite group of six bright-field TEM micrographs of 0.5C steel (Fe–18Mn–10Al–0.5C) after tensile deformation of a duplex austenite (γ) + ferrite (α) structure, each panel lettered (a)–(f) in its top-left corner and carrying a scale bar in its bottom-right corner. (a) and (b) are the low-strain condition, true strain ε = 0.02: (a) shows parallel, straight planar slip traces crossing an austenite grain; (b) shows a ferrite region with coarse dislocation tangles gathered around a subgrain/cell boundary. (c)–(f) are the higher-strain condition, ε = 0.18. In austenite, (c) shows intensive closely spaced dislocation slip on several systems, (d) shows a Taylor lattice — a near-rectangular grid of intersecting dislocation walls, and (e) shows dark elongated microbands running diagonally. In ferrite, (f) shows dense, heavily overlapping dislocation tangles. Scale bars read 0.2 µm in (a), (b), (c), (e) and (f), but 0.5 µm in (d). No magnification or axis values are printed. Together the panels demonstrate progressive slip localisation with strain — planar slip and isolated tangles at ε = 0.02, then Taylor lattices plus microbands in austenite and dense tangles in ferrite at ε = 0.18 — the microstructural basis of the two-stage strain hardening reported for 0.5C steel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM of austenite (γ) at ε = 0.02 showing parallel straight planar slip traces intersecting across the grain; 0.2 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of ferrite (α) at ε = 0.02 showing coarse dislocation tangles concentrated around a subgrain/cell boundary; 0.2 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of austenite (γ) at ε = 0.18 showing intensive dislocation slip with closely spaced slip lines on multiple systems; 0.2 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of austenite (γ) at ε = 0.18 showing a Taylor lattice, i.e. two sets of intersecting dislocation walls forming a rectangular grid within the subgrain; 0.5 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of austenite (γ) at ε = 0.18 showing dark elongated microbands aligned diagonally across the field; 0.2 µm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of ferrite (α) at ε = 0.18 showing dense, heavily overlapping dislocation tangles with no clear cell structure; 0.2 µm scale bar.

observations.observation: The figure contains six bright-field TEM micrographs lettered (a) to (f), each with a scale bar in the lower-right corner.
Scale bars read 0.2 µm in panels (a), (b), (c), (e) and (f), while panel (d) has a 0.5 µm scale bar.
Panel (a) displays straight, parallel planar slip lines crossing an austenite grain at low strain.
Panel (b) displays coarsely tangled dislocations gathered around a subgrain/cell boundary in ferrite.
Panel (d) displays a near-rectangular grid formed by two intersecting sets of dislocation walls, the Taylor lattice.
Panel (e) displays dark, elongated bands (microbands) oriented diagonally across the imaged region.
Panel (f) displays dense, heavily overlapped dislocation tangles with no resolvable cell walls.
The caption states that panels (a)–(b) correspond to true strain ε 0.02 and panels (c)–(f) to ε 0.18.
The caption assigns (a) planar slip (γ), (b) dislocation tangles (α), (c) intensive dislocation slip (γ), (d) Taylor lattice (γ), (e) microbands (γ) and (f) dense dislocation tangles (α).
The citing text states that a two-stage strain hardening is observed for 0.5C steel, and that in the first stage planar slip in austenite starts while dislocation tangles form in ferrite.

The citing text states that in the second stage a low-energy Taylor lattice structure and microbands develop in austenite, with more dislocation tangles forming in ferrite, resulting in relatively high strain hardening.
The citing text reports multi-slip in austenite of 0.5C steel even at low strain, contrasting with dominant single slip in 0.8C steel (Fig. 7(a)).

unreadable_items: No magnification values are printed on any panel; only scale bars are given.
The crystallographic indices of the slip systems in (a) and (c) are not labelled.
